correctness.rationale: For all positive a,b, the product of two greedy subsequence DFAs has exactly four explicitly described, pairwise disjoint reachable regions, each with constructive witness words. Their size sums to n(n+3)/2+ab. Four probe families recover both coordinates under intersection, proving every reachable state distinguishable; four analogous probes recover both coordinates of every nonaccepting union state, while exactly n+1 accepting states are all equivalent to the same absorbing right language, giving union size R-n. The standalone checker replayed 324 parameter pairs and 65,520 independent direct-subsequence word comparisons; those finite tests supplement, not substitute for, the proof. The only assumptions are a,b positive and the fixed binary alphabet.

value.rationale: Intersection and union of principal scattered-subsequence ideals are natural model-composition operations highlighted by current research in automata decomposition. The intrinsic independent parameters are the lengths of the initial zero and one blocks; the new exact formulas cover every positive pair and reveal a nontrivial mixed ab contribution and a precise, structurally explained gap of a+b states. Their explicit reachable geometry and distinguishing suffix families provide parametric minimal automata, not a numerical example or a substitution into existing generic upper bounds.
